prerequisites: Review of electronics and semiconductor knowledge from undergraduate studies, particularly electronic devices and constitutive blocks of digital systems (wired and programmed logic).

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the different semicustom and fullcustom integrated circuit design technologies.
Know the different integrated circuit manufacturing processes.
Know the different phases of semicustom integrated circuit design.
Design fullcustom combinational circuits according to manufacturer's design rules.
Functionally simulate the design of a combinational circuit.
Design fullcustom sequential circuits according to manufacturer's design rules.
Functionally simulate the design of a sequential circuit.
Design and simulate simple analog circuits, such as two-stage operational amplifiers.
Understand the legal aspects and commitments related to the design and manufacture of integrated circuits.

syllabus_topics: Technological factors, environmental considerations, and future trends
The MOS transistor: models and equivalent circuits
Design of combinational and sequential circuits
assessment_rules: The evaluation system is the same for all calls. The main evaluation consists of a theory exam (65%), practice reports (10%), and an individual project (25%). For differentiated evaluation, the theory exam accounts for 65% and a practice exam for 35%. The theory exam covers the course material. The practice exam involves performing parts of the completed practical exercises.
